title: Naming Rules and Identifiers
learningObjectives: Recognize its syntax and important rules.
Explain the sample programs and predict their results.
Use this concept in a small program.
Identify common mistakes and choose a safer approach.

understand.concept: An identifier is a name used for program entities such as variables and functions. C++ identifiers may contain letters, digits and underscores, cannot begin with a digit, and cannot be a keyword. Names are case-sensitive.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct data declarations and type choices make C++ programs easier to understand, safer and more portable.
understand.explain: Choose descriptive names that communicate meaning. Avoid leading underscores in names you define because some forms are reserved to the implementation. Prefer consistent style such as lowerCamelCase or snake_case within a project.
